{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement (we are the Customer)

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The commercial architecture of the deal is, in several respects, materially adverse to us and includes four terms that fall into walk-away territory as our playbook defines it.

The most serious problem is structural: **the Agreement has no indemnification article at all.** Sections 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 29.2 and 30.5 all cross-refer to indemnities that do not exist (Section 9.3 points to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" and there is no Section 20). With no Vendor IP indemnity, we carry third-party infringement risk on a hosted service we do not own.

Alongside that, **Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable we pay for**, leaving us only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — so our right to use work product built specifically for us simply ends on expiry.

We are also asked to accept a cluster of one-sided restrictions on our own freedom of action that our playbook does not permit at any level: a **three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights"** (§ 2.1), a **24-month all-territory non-compete and no-hire covenant** (§ 12.4), and a **disclose-and-match MFN obligation running in Vendor's favour** (§ 7.2). Notably, each of these directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. The internal inconsistency is helpful to us in negotiation and should make these edits easier to land as conforming clean-up.

Two further gaps warrant attention: there is **no termination-for-convenience right** for either party, and **no transition-assistance or data-return obligation** on exit — a significant omission in a hosting arrangement. Governing law is also misdrafted: § 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which conflicts with § 28.2's exclusive New York County forum.

On the positive side, the risk-allocation and operational provisions are strong. Limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal and price escalation (§ 8), warranties (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all meet our preferred position, and several contain terms that actively favour us. We are not proposing changes to any of those.

**Overall:** 8 items require redlines (3 critical, 4 high, 4 medium — with § 2.1 and § 12.4 each engaging two rules), and 10 items are compliant and require no action.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | Indemnification by Vendor (INDEMN) | **Missing** | § 9.3 (dangling reference to Section 20.5) | No indemnification article exists anywhere; multiple sections presuppose indemnities that were never drafted. Walk-away. |
| Critical | Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP) | **Deviation** | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; we hold only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails the fallback. |
| Critical | Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs (LOL-CAP) | Compliant | § 21.1 | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full preferred carve-out set in § 21.3. |
| High | Non-compete restrictions on Customer (NONCOMPETE) | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | Term plus 24 months, "any product or service that competes", "any territory", bars acquisitions. Walk-away. |
| High | Non-solicitation of employees (NOSOLICIT) | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-sided 24-month no-hire covering any Vendor employee, expressly defeating general-advertising carve-outs. Walk-away. |
| High | Termination for convenience (T4C) | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | No convenience right for either party; § 2.1 affirmatively strips termination rights across the three-year commitment. Walk-away. |
| High | Assignment and change of control (ASSIGN) | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free assignment to Affiliate or successor; § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate or reprice on our change of control. |
| High | Exclusivity obligations binding Customer (EXCLUSIVITY) | Compliant | § 12.3 | No sourcing exclusivity; § 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to engage any supplier. |
| High | Liquidated damages and penalties (LD) | Compliant | § 27.3 | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee payable by us; § 27.3 permits termination "without penalty". |
| High | Licence grant scope (LICENSE) | Compliant | § 13.1 | Worldwide licence extending to Affiliates and contractors; § 13.2 perpetual and irrevocable for paid-up software. |
| Medium | Minimum purchase commitments (MINCOMMIT) | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | USD 2,000,000 per year for three years, take-or-pay, no reduction right. Walk-away; contradicts § 12.3 and sits uneasily with § 7.1. |
| Medium | Most-favoured-nation obligations (MFN) | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | We must disclose and match any more favourable offer for Vendor's benefit — no product scope, time limit or like-for-like carve-outs. Walk-away. |
| Medium | Governing law and venue (GOVLAW) | **Deviation** | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction; outside the accepted list and conflicts with § 28.2's New York forum. |
| Medium | Post-termination transition assistance and data return (TRANSITION) | **Missing** | § 10.1 | No transition-assistance or data return/export/deletion obligation; § 10.1 assumes a transition period without requiring one. |
| Medium | Audit rights against Customer (AUDIT) | Compliant | § 22.1 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, independent auditor; no direct system access (§ 22.2). |
| Medium | Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window (RENEWAL) | Compliant | § 8.2 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension; § 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | Performance warranty and duration (WARRANTY) | Compliant | § 19.1 | Workmanlike and conformity warranties with no durational cut-off; mutual disclaimer does not limit express warranties. |
| Low | Vendor insurance (INSURANCE) | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL, E&O USD 2m, cyber and privacy USD 5m, term plus one year; certificates on request under § 18.2. |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following five terms sit in walk-away territory under our playbook and must be resolved before signature:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing Section 20).** With no IP indemnity at all, we bear third-party infringement risk. We are inserting Section 20 at the preferred level: defence and indemnity for us and our Affiliates covering IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control of defence and cooperation, and our own indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. We have not adopted the fallback because its 3x annual-fee super-cap would cut back the uncapped treatment of indemnification obligations that § 21.3's Excluded Claims already gives us. Section 9.3's reference to Section 20.5 remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund) remains and can be conformed if Vendor prefers the fallback structure.

2. **Three-year take-or-pay with no exit (§ 2.1).** USD 2,000,000 per year for three years, expressly without reduction or termination rights, fails every fallback element. We propose replacing it with a no-minimum-commitment, pay-for-use provision; no other clause cross-refers to it, so it can be excised cleanly.

3. **24-month non-compete and no-hire (§ 12.4).** The post-term tail exceeds 12 months, the scope is undefined and territory-wide, and there are no carve-outs for internal development, acquisitions or general advertising. Both covenants are removed. A mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with customary carve-outs and no no-hire element, remains available as a fallback if Vendor pushes back.

4. **Customer-side MFN (§ 7.2).** An open-ended obligation to disclose and match any more favourable offer, with no defined product, time limit or like-for-like comparison. We are converting it into an express statement that no such obligation exists. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing in our favour is affected.

5. **Singapore law and exclusive Singapore forum (§ 28.1).** Outside our accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and in direct conflict with § 28.2. We propose New York law in § 28.1 and deletion of the Singapore forum words, leaving § 28.2's exclusive New York County forum intact.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviation and missing items: new Section 20 (Vendor indemnity), Section 14.2 (Deliverable ownership flipped to us with a Vendor assignment, and the redundant revocable licence dropped), Section 2.1 (no-minimum pay-for-use, and removal of the termination-rights bar), new Section 9.4 (30-day Customer convenience exit with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and a bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term), Section 12.4 (both covenants removed), Section 7.2 (MFN obligation negated), Section 28.1 (New York law), and new Section 10.3 (up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion after return).

2. **Lead with the internal inconsistencies.** Sections 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict § 12.3, and § 28.1 contradicts § 28.2. Framing these edits as conforming clean-up rather than commercial re-trading should shorten the negotiation.

3. **Flag the drafting gap on indemnities to Vendor's counsel directly.** The five existing cross-references to a non-existent Section 20 suggest an article was dropped in assembly; this is likely to be conceded quickly.

4. **Confirm the commercial position on § 2.1 with the business team.** If a volume commitment is genuinely part of the negotiated price, we need instructions on an acceptable structure before we table the no-minimum edit; our fallback analysis assumes no commitment was agreed.

5. **Hold the compliant items.** We are not redlining Sections 8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 or 27, and should resist any Vendor attempt to reopen them (in particular the § 21.3 Excluded Claims and the § 24.4 change-of-control protection) as consideration for the changes above.

6. **Two minor points noted, not redlined:** the § 12.4 competitor bar in the assignment clause is limited to a "direct" competitor, and the standalone Deliverable conformity period in § 19.2 is 90 days rather than 12 months. Neither is worth raising given the surrounding protections; we can pick them up if the document reopens for other reasons.

---

*All findings above are drawn from the verified review record. No section references or conclusions have been extrapolated beyond it.*"}
